name: RE-Bench
intro: RE-Bench（Research Engineering Benchmark）是多个 Gemini 和 OpenAI 报告引用的 AI 研发任务评测，用于衡量模型在真实研究工程问题上的代理能力。
intro_en: RE-Bench, the Research Engineering Benchmark, is cited by Gemini and OpenAI reports for evaluating AI research and engineering agent tasks.
drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; status=source-reconstructed-awaiting-independent-signoff; scope=RE-Bench v1 paper-aligned bilingual Build Process, iterative environment creation, human and agent evaluation, per-run scoring, normalization, best-of-k aggregation, official-release boundary, MIT license, and separate informal contamination request. Primary evidence is RE-Bench v2 at https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.15114v2 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.15114v2; the reviewed PDF SHA-256 is 9d25c5ea6abfeeb40b5c8fa7a8e637cd8785d2a0f022f2798c33769af8d66992. Official implementation evidence is pinned to https://github.com/METR/RE-Bench/tree/93b98062e55f6945d4a7e213a3226dd419896170. The paper begins from three early-warning evaluation goals: feasibility, ecological validity, and resistance to saturation, while directly comparing human experts and AI agents. Candidate ideas come from discussions with ML practitioners, relevant literature, and prior METR work. The disclosed creation process has three iterative stages. Specification writes and reworks an environment description, scoring function, and starting solution until the authors expect the proposal to cover important AI R&D challenges, permit steady expert progress toward a high ceiling, and remain practical to implement. Implementation builds the full environment plus an internal strong solution and reworks them against the same requirements. Baselining runs human experts, observes whether the environment works in practice, and often makes significant adjustments. Candidates can return for rework or be dropped. During development the team discarded more than 12 specifications at varying completion levels and more than five completed implementations. The retained RE-Bench v1 contract contains seven hand-crafted, open-ended ML research-engineering environments: Optimize LLM Foundry, Optimize a Kernel, Fix Embedding, Scaling Law Experiment, Restricted Architecture MLM, Finetune GPT-2 for QA, and Scaffolding for Rust Codecontests. Every environment includes instructions and resources, a scoring function, a simple but poorly performing starting solution visible to the participant, and a high-scoring reference solution hidden from the participant. The reference solution supplies normalization evidence and is not an agent input. Human evidence consists of 71 eight-hour attempts by 61 distinct experts under the environment conditions. AI agents are also run with wall-clock budgets in the same task interfaces. During a run, participants edit files, run code and experiments, and may call the scorer, which appends timestamped entries to a score log. Per-run scoring has a critical branch: in all environments except Scaling Law Experiment, the assessed result is the highest score registered in the log by run end; in Scaling Law Experiment the participant cannot see the achieved score and only the final submission counts. Raw task score y is normalized against starting score ys and hidden reference score yr using yn = (y - ys) / (yr - ys). A solution worse than the starting solution is assigned 0. Scores greater than 1 are explicitly allowed because a solution may beat the reference. The normalized values make results comparable across the seven tasks. For score@k, the paper samples k run results with replacement within each environment. Standard environments select the highest sampled score. Scaling Law cannot support score-aware selection, so one sampled result is selected randomly. The report averages normalized score across the seven environments and compares human and agent performance. This graph does not collapse per-run highest-log selection into best-of-k; they are separate operations. At fixed commit 93b98062e55f6945d4a7e213a3226dd419896170, suite_manifest.yaml enumerates seven task families and has SHA-256 0f6205a46c61a26e7476e498a4199b7d2a3ee4abf53c27dbb7f3640ddcd008ff. README.md SHA-256 is 7f279f6fcbfa8d6e7309764cd7620f682ffbeaedc5f9af09b8746b9c10bbb2dd. The repository is MIT licensed; LICENSE SHA-256 is 0651c2b4111fb02dcf9dee40b78f51a44d72f1ed53129d914a18ba6b0fe07312. The repository additionally makes an informal request to reduce training-data contamination, overfitting, and publication of unprotected solutions. That request is shown as a separate non-binding release boundary rather than being rewritten as an extra MIT condition. No credential, password, protected-solution content, private artifact, hidden reference solution, or secrets-file content is reproduced in this graph or note. English and Chinese specs have identical semantic IDs, types, sizes, positions, styles, edge endpoints, edge types, edge styles, waypoints, and modules; every secondary edge explicitly sets dashed=true and no edge has a label. Canonical source/spec/architecture and SVG paths remain unchanged; mermaid_flowchart is null and both legacy fallbacks are empty. Strict Draw.io/XML and runtime visual review are required next; replacement formal assets and refreshed paper_aligned registration remain gated on independent reviewer approval.
